errors.means: desk-web serves only browser_context and browser_command, and the name called is neither.
errors.fix: Call tools/list on desk-web and use one of the two names it lists.

doors.when: Before any page work, to get a contextId for a headless Edge or Chrome, or to end one and remove its temporary folder

errors.means: Opening mine, the operating system refused to let Desk read the person's browser profile, so no copy was opened.
errors.fix: Open a fresh browser instead; only the person can grant that access in the system's privacy settings.

errors.means: Opening mine, a required profile file could not be qualified (identity, single link or readable bytes), so no copy was opened.
errors.fix: Open a fresh browser instead; don't work around the refusal by controlling the person's own browser.

errors.means: close named a mine context this server doesn't own, such as one an earlier Desk process opened.
errors.fix: Leave that context alone and open a new one; each server closes only the contexts it opened.

errors.means: Closing a mine context, its cleanup couldn't be confirmed, so its private files were kept.
errors.fix: Call desk_doctor to see Desk's runtime state, and report it if the close fails again.

errors.means: Any other refusal: no Edge or Chrome installed, the browser driver didn't install, or a bad action or contextId.
errors.fix: Read the message, which names the cause and the next step, such as installing a browser or passing open's contextId.

doors.when: After browser_context opens a context, for each page step: navigating, reading the accessibility tree, clicking, typing, taking pictures

errors.means: In mine, the page replaced or navigated away from the element since its ref was read.
errors.fix: Run ["snapshot"] again and act on a fresh ref; while a page loads, run ["wait","<text you expect>"] first.

errors.means: In mine, the ref isn't from one of the tab's recent reads, or its element has gone.
errors.fix: Take a new snapshot and use a ref from it.

errors.means: In mine, args[0] isn't one of the commands mine runs; the message lists them.
errors.fix: Use a listed command, or eval or run-code for anything the list doesn't cover.

errors.means: In mine, the command ran out of time, and Desk closed the context.
errors.fix: Open a new context with browser_context and start again from the page you were on, keeping waits under a minute.

errors.means: No open browser has that contextId, args aren't a list of strings or start with no page command, or a fresh command failed or ran too long.
errors.fix: Read the message, which names the cause: open a context first, fix args, or run the command again.

errors.means: Desk's browser hit an unexpected problem with no safer message to give.
errors.fix: Call the tool again; if it repeats, call friction_add with the code.
